batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 distinct candidate IDs and their exact packet-supplied premeasurement V1/V2 predictions as one batch. Prioritize unresolved structure-condition relationships: late completion in weak eluent, endpoint-specific loading responses, and the confounded m125 loading-volume contrasts. Add targeted nitrogen and nitro-carbonyl response measurements and two matched solvent pairs on unmeasured aromatic carbonyl scaffolds. Current predictions, historical acquisition errors and chemical priors are treated as separate evidence sources.

choices.reason: m125 at 2/1, 150 mg and 300 uL DCM supplies one missing corner between c8d43713db33bf820a1d (100 mg, 300 uL; 15.41/29.58 mL) and facbcedbecb46072b04c (150 mg, 500 uL; 32.95/69.81 mL). It helps distinguish loading from injection-volume effects or variability behind this large discrepancy.

m125 at 2/1, 100 mg and 500 uL DCM supplies the other missing corner of the loading-by-volume comparison. Together with the selected 150 mg/300 uL row and observations c8d43713db33bf820a1d and facbcedbecb46072b04c, it tests effects that the current predictions essentially ignore.

m125 at 1/1, 100 mg and 500 uL DCM isolates loading-solvent volume against 4c32851430464f0ed684 and loading against 9bd998a328b109ef639e. Connecting this point to the selected same-load 2/1 row tests whether the unexplained differences depend on mobile-phase strength.

m118 at 20/1 and 56.05 mg directly contrasts loading with fc27fa779102c4aeb8ab at 112.1 mg. The same scaffold subsequently exposed a 50.58 mL historical V2 underprediction at 50/1 in 2d178efe0181baca2bd5. This tests loading transfer within a steep weak-eluent response.

m118 at 5/1 and 168.15 mg pairs directly with measured 10/1 row ea004678fc850c759752 at identical loading conditions. Its current prediction is about 11.72/25.17 mL. This anchors the earlier part of the solvent curve after failures at weaker eluent, without transferring those failures as a constant offset.

Methyl acetoacetate at 10/1 and 107.6 mg matches the loading of 1a55639d058c08a1a06e at 50/1, whose V2 was historically underpredicted by 43.16 mL. The intermediate label tests where the unexpectedly late completion develops; the current prediction is about 15.29/36.00 mL.

Methyl acetoacetate at 20/1 and 53.8 mg extends the fixed-load 2/1 and 5/1 anchors 8d018e521e8e6bbc53c2 and cd566862a517dd7cdc8d. With the selected high-load 20/1 partner, it tests both response curvature and whether loading changes onset more than completion.

Methyl acetoacetate at 20/1 and 161.4 mg triples the loading of its selected 20/1 partner while holding the remaining conditions fixed. The predictor gives almost identical endpoints across these loads. Measurements can test whether the onset advances seen in other retained beta-ketoesters transfer to this simpler scaffold.

Ethyl acetoacetate at 20/1 and 102.9 mg tests transfer from the newly identified methyl-acetoacetate weak-eluent failure. Its current prediction is about 19.04/45.48 mL. Observations cd2c80dae2f32a52732f and 3ad8ec5752f3c638e2ff anchor 5/1 at a higher load, so their loading difference remains explicit.

tert-Butyl acetoacetate at 10/1 and 95.4 mg matches the loading and injection conditions of 50/1 observation 3fc05dc2025715e68174, measured at 42.22/88.03 mL. It tests the intermediate solvent slope across ester substitution and helps constrain transfer from methyl, ethyl and ether-containing acetoacetates.

m78 at 20/1 and 51.8 mg halves the loading of a44a22945d76c02aa6a7. Its selected same-load 50/1 partner creates a matched solvent comparison. This extends the loading-response experiment below the existing 103.6 and 155.4 mg weak-eluent observations.

m78 at 50/1 and 51.8 mg tests whether lower loading gives later onset while completion remains near the roughly 98-99 mL measured in 61771d230b285babe4b6 and eb3bc3fba39e57adbc2f. The current prediction, about 41.45/81.12 mL, does not reproduce that proposed endpoint-specific transfer.

m200 at 1/1 and 193.755 mg completes the three-load 1/1 series beside 97318de99bab4460cf4e and 7dace1dbecce79e17117. The corresponding high-load 2/1 result f91285c618eacb53538b showed earlier onset than lower loads. This tests whether loading sensitivity contracts in stronger eluent.

Cyano-substituted benzophenone m159 at 50/1 and 100 mg extends the matched 20/1 observation a738b1f204da6fcfd385, measured at 21.33/51.94 mL. Its prediction is about 31.16/71.76 mL. The label tests whether late weak-eluent completion transfers to a nitrile-carbonyl topology after the m118 and m178 failures.

Nitroacetophenone m37 at 20/1 preserves the loading of 10/1 observation 38e6b8bf0f089fcadd80, measured at 25.64/55.08 mL. The current 32.32/78.22 mL prediction and broad quantile spans identify an untested weaker-eluent region. This is a useful comparison with the selected nitroaldehyde points.

Para-nitrobenzaldehyde at 20/1 and 149.6 mg extends the matched 2/1 and 5/1 observations f9564b598f30f816ac19 and 6ae922f63e983b14e320. The model predicts about 33.13/82.47 mL, a substantial rise beyond measured 5/1 completion of 28.03 mL. Measuring it tests the predicted transition directly.

Ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde at 20/1 and 150 mg pairs with its selected 2/1 point and pure-EA observation 3232c07325c3dd8f1e6a. The predicted 18.73/53.70 mL differs considerably from the para-isomer prediction. Similar masses support comparison, but the isomers use different DCM volumes, preventing a clean positional attribution.

Ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde at 2/1 preserves the 150 mg loading and 300 uL DCM of 3232c07325c3dd8f1e6a and the selected 20/1 row. This stronger-eluent anchor separates a scaffold-specific solvent slope from a simple retention offset and makes the weak-eluent measurement more interpretable.

Para-amino ethyl benzoate at 5/1 and 117 mg doubles the loading of c70b471334f9747d6f98, measured at 32.05/58.38 mL. With the selected low-load 2/1 point and existing 2/1 anchor 70593725787c65a74951, it completes a two-ratio, two-load comparison.

Para-amino ethyl benzoate at 2/1 and 58.5 mg matches the loading of c70b471334f9747d6f98 at 5/1 and halves that of 70593725787c65a74951 at 2/1. This tests solvent-response transfer across loading in an aniline ester whose completion was recently overpredicted.

Ortho-amino ethyl benzoate at 20/1 tests whether the relatively early 5/1 behavior in 3aed7873d2fd1cf48684 and 18186b5d6cc190fc07a3 persists as eluent weakens. Its 111.7 mg loading lies between those measured loads. Comparison with para/meta amino esters must also retain their different loading solvents and injection volumes.

Diphenyl sulfoxide at 5/1 and 150 mg directly contrasts loading with 714004602e6452764d9a at 100 mg. It also supplies the matched loading anchor for the selected 10/1 row, allowing the model's predicted completion flattening to be tested without confounding mobile-phase strength with loading.

Methylquinoline m146 at 5/1 and 54.15 mg extends the fixed-loading 1/1 observation b6229f0445560a4a54ed. Its current prediction is about 24.67/50.94 mL. This tests solvent-response transfer among fused aromatic bases; comparison with quinoline 33ffc69a253a89f15995 has a loading difference.

Quinoline at 2/1 and 109.3 mg matches all loading conditions of 5/1 observation 33ffc69a253a89f15995, measured at 27.90/57.67 mL. The predicted contraction to about 11.58/30.97 mL tests the strong-to-moderate eluent transition for a basic ring nitrogen.

2,6-Lutidine at 20/1 and 138 mg extends 2/1 observation 8436939a2a6a91fa470d at identical loading conditions. Its predicted 28.99/55.62 mL tests weak-eluent extrapolation for a sterically substituted pyridine and provides a useful boundary for corrections learned from pyridyl carbonyls and fused bases.

Diphenyl sulfoxide at 10/1 and 150 mg pairs with the selected 5/1 row. The model predicts completion near 47.73 mL, below its selected 5/1 prediction of 49.19 mL despite weaker eluent. The pair discriminates genuine response flattening from model underfitting, with measured context from 714004602e6452764d9a.

Dibenzylideneacetone m164 at 20/1 fills a fixed-loading gap between 1/1 observation 3f6b817d855e67b3b406 and 50/1 observation c9bef93a79964dc6ede1. The current prediction is about 13.03/36.12 mL. This tests how an extended conjugated single-carbonyl topology enters its late-elution regime.

Unmeasured ortho-methylbenzaldehyde at 5/1 supplies the stronger-eluent member of a matched 103.9 mg, 300 uL DCM pair. It anchors transfer from measured substituted aldehydes before interpreting the selected 50/1 result. Steric shielding is a chemical hypothesis, not an established finding for this molecule.

Ortho-methylbenzaldehyde at 50/1 matches the selected 5/1 loading conditions. Its predicted 11.34/22.91 mL represents a modest solvent response. The pair tests whether this transfers to a new positional environment, informed by related aldehyde observations such as 44500edb95a3649adf91 and the varied aromatic-carbonyl slopes elsewhere in L_t.

Para-methoxybenzophenone at 50/1 and 100 mg tests transfer of late weak-eluent completion to another methoxy aromatic carbonyl. Its measured 1/1 anchors d89efcf911f250d9ecf3 and 70d035703d3eaebf81e6 finish near 11 mL at different loads. The new label can prevent overgeneralizing either the m118 failure or the modest benzophenone response.

Unmeasured biphenyl-containing aryl butanone m68 at 5/1 anchors a matched solvent pair at 102.2 mg and 400 uL DCM. It tests structural transfer into an extended hydrophobic aryl ketone while retaining a carbonyl adsorption site. This complements the already measured neutral biphenyl references.

m68 at 50/1 matches its selected 5/1 partner; predictions rise from about 4.66/12.26 to 12.49/30.46 mL. The pair tests whether aromatic extension and carbonyl environment change the solvent slope beyond what transfers from simpler aryl ketones. Neutral biphenyl d0c3cf60cb8fef1f9e7d supplies context, with loading conditions explicitly different.

hypotheses.content: Several retained scaffolds show earlier onset at higher sample loading, with a smaller change in completion. This relationship appears solvent- and scaffold-dependent; the irregular m177 series does not support a universal smooth loading law.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Current candidate predictions are nearly invariant to loading. Matched contrasts can teach endpoint-specific effects and their solvent dependence without imposing the same correction on every molecule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do lower-load m78 and methyl acetoacetate show later onset without a proportional completion shift, and do the m200, amino-ester and sulfoxide contrasts change with solvent strength?

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent completion and the location of steep solvent-response transitions depend strongly on carbonyl and ester topology. A response learned for one aromatic carbonyl or acetoacetate cannot safely be transferred as a common slope or offset.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recent large completion underpredictions identify incompletely learned response curves. Intermediate-ratio labels and comparisons across ester substitution, conjugation and aromatic substituents can repair relationships shared by many catalog rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does late completion emerge between ordinary and weak PE/EA mixtures, and which response features transfer among methyl, ethyl, tert-butyl and substituted acetoacetates or among different aromatic carbonyl topologies?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing families have distinct solvent responses that require joint modeling of nitrogen identity, position, surrounding functionality and recorded loading conditions. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding or steric shielding in ortho-amino esters remains a chemical explanation to test, not an observed mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Amino esters, amino nitriles, secondary amines and aromatic bases cannot share a generic nitrogen-retention correction. Local solvent and loading contrasts can improve transfer while respecting confounded cross-molecule comparisons.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the para-amino ester response reproduce across two loads, does the ortho-amino ester retain its relatively early behavior in weaker eluent, and how do substituted pyridines and fused bases approach their strong-eluent regimes?

hypotheses.content: The predicted weak-eluent transitions of nitroacetophenone and nitrobenzaldehydes, including the predicted ortho/para difference, are unresolved. Nitro-carbonyl topology may alter response slopes, but existing anchors do not establish the proposed 20/1 behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These candidates occupy a poorly tested response region with large predicted changes. Matched within-molecule solvent measurements can distinguish real transitions from extrapolation artifacts; cross-isomer comparisons remain limited by different injection volumes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the large predicted 20/1 increases supported, and does the ortho-nitroaldehyde show a different within-molecule solvent slope from the para analogue after retaining the recorded-condition differences?

hypotheses.content: The m125 observations do not establish a single sharp 1/1-to-2/1 transition independent of loading conditions. Large differences between the 100 mg/300 uL and 150 mg/500 uL series may reflect loading, injection-volume interactions or variability; their contributions are unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest opposite-signed acquisition errors exposed a confounded condition relationship, while current predictions remain almost insensitive to loading-solvent volume. Missing factorial corners can identify whether corrections should attach to solvent strength, loading conditions or variable observations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1, which endpoints follow loading versus DCM volume when both missing corners are measured, and does the isolated volume contrast at 1/1 show the same pattern?

hypotheses.content: Solvent-response transfer to unmeasured ortho-methylbenzaldehyde and the biphenyl-containing aryl ketone is uncertain. Steric environment, aromatic extension and carbonyl attachment may change adsorption and response slopes beyond a simple lipophilicity adjustment.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Two matched solvent pairs provide structural exploration with interpretable condition responses, potentially improving predictions for related unmeasured aromatic rows rather than supplying isolated new-molecule offsets.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do these new scaffolds exhibit the modest predicted 5/1-to-50/1 changes, or do their carbonyl environments produce substantially different onset and completion slopes?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes strengthen the need for topology-specific weak-eluent learning. m118 at 50/1 finished at 117.46 mL, exposing a 50.58 mL acquisition-time V2 underprediction (2d178efe0181baca2bd5); methyl acetoacetate finished at 76.31 mL with a 43.16 mL historical underprediction (1a55639d058c08a1a06e). I therefore reject the earlier expectation that the simple methyl-acetoacetate weak-eluent response would necessarily be modest and select intermediate ratios plus ester-family comparisons. Loading follow-ups now provide a coherent pattern across several molecules: m107 onset moved earlier at higher loading at both 2/1 and 5/1 while completion changed less; m200 at 2/1 also showed progressively earlier onset with comparatively stable completion. m78 and amino-nitrile results support related endpoint-specific contrasts, although m177 remains a counterexample to a universal loading law. The m125 results weaken the previously predicted transition location: the 100 mg/300 uL 2/1 row completed at 29.58 mL, whereas the existing 150 mg/500 uL row completed at 69.81 mL. Because both loading and DCM volume differ, I now prioritize missing comparison corners rather than attribute the discrepancy to mobile-phase strength alone. Dibenzylamine at 10/1 eluted substantially later than predicted, showing why its earlier 5/1 overprediction should not induce a common negative correction across conditions. The m205 pure-EA result supports the measured strong-eluent contraction already seen for m206, reducing the value of further generic pure-EA alcohol exploration. Recent m32 extensions and m177 stronger-eluent points mostly had smaller acquisition errors, so they receive less immediate follow-up. Historical errors are not current-model residuals, and the supplied endpoint-order anomalies remain uninterpreted as physical negative elution intervals.
batch_rationale: All 32 choices are distinct eligible candidate IDs, with no pending experiments in this free arm. The batch combines repair of recently exposed response failures with experiments that can teach transferable interactions. The m125 measurements fill missing loading-volume comparisons instead of assuming a solvent-only explanation. Methyl acetoacetate, ethyl and tert-butyl analogues, m118 and other carbonyl topologies test the onset of late completion across solvent strength. The low-load m78 pair, high-load m200 point, amino-ester comparison and matched sulfoxide pair examine loading effects that current predictions largely suppress. Nitrogen and nitro-carbonyl selections test distinct chemical environments and unmeasured transitions rather than apply one polarity or nitrogen correction. Two new aromatic carbonyl scaffolds each receive a matched solvent pair so exploration yields a response relationship rather than only a single anchor. More acceptor-free aromatic measurements are deprioritized because the recent biphenyl panel showed relatively modest errors; similarly, additional strong-eluent measurements on already corrected alcohols and irregular m177 rows have less expected marginal value here. Numerical distance and quantile spans inform attention but do not determine selection: several useful matched contrasts have low CW distance, and the quantile spans come from one predictor and are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty. V2-V1 is treated as elution interval width. These labels may improve overall Row accuracy by teaching scaffold-specific solvent slopes, endpoint-specific loading effects and recorded-condition interactions across recurring chemical families. Observed variability, differing injection conditions in some cross-molecule comparisons and absent experimental variables limit causal interpretation and the certainty of the expected retraining benefit.
